record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: blow-up set of unbounded extremal solutions
record.original_question: For the extremal solution u^* of the nonlinear Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda f(u) in a smooth bounded domain, assume u^* is not essentially bounded. What can be said about the blow-up set of u^*? In particular, when Omega is convex, must the blow-up set consist of a single point?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.2 ([16, 34]). Assume u^* is not in L^infinity(Omega). What can be said about the blow-up set of u^*? Does it consist of a single point when Omega is convex?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a smooth bounded domain, and let $f:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a $C^1$, nondecreasing, convex, superlinear nonlinearity (i.e. $f(0)>0$ and $\lim_{t\to\infty} f(t)/t = +\infty$). Consider the family of semilinear Dirichlet problems
$$-\Delta u = \lambda\, f(u) \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u>0 \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u=0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
indexed by $\lambda>0$. It is classical that there is a finite extremal parameter $\lambda^*\in(0,\infty)$ such that for $\lambda\in(0,\lambda^*)$ this problem admits a minimal classical solution $u_\lambda$, and the pointwise increasing limit
$$u^*(x) := \lim_{\lambda\nearrow\lambda^*} u_\lambda(x)$$
defines a weak ("extremal") solution at $\lambda=\lambda^*$. Define the blow-up set of $u^*$ as
$$\mathcal{B}(u^*) := \{x_0\in\overline{\Omega} : \operatorname{ess\,sup}_{B_r(x_0)\cap\Omega} u^* = +\infty \text{ for every } r>0\}.$$

Assume that $u^*\notin L^\infty(\Omega)$.

(a) Describe the structure of $\mathcal{B}(u^*)$ (size, regularity, possible locations) under general assumptions on $\Omega$ and $f$.

(b) When $\Omega$ is in addition convex, must $\mathcal{B}(u^*)$ consist of a single point?
artifact.category_tag: Extremal solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
artifact.status_search_result: No publication establishing a general structure theorem for the blow-up set of unbounded extremal solutions, nor a proof that the blow-up set is a single point on convex domains, was located. The question is stated as an open problem in surveys on extremal solutions and no resolution appears in the recent literature found.

status_evidence.title: Blow-up solutions of some nonlinear elliptic problems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses blow-up phenomena in nonlinear elliptic problems without resolving the single-point conjecture for extremal solutions on convex domains.
status_evidence.claim: Literature on blow-up sets of nonlinear elliptic problems does not contain a resolution of the single-point blow-up conjecture for extremal solutions on convex domains.

status_evidence.title: Elliptic Problems with Nonlinear Boundary Conditions and the Sobolev Trace Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on extremal solutions and regularity questions; the structure of the blow-up set when the extremal solution is unbounded is mentioned as not fully understood.
status_evidence.claim: The structure of the blow-up set of unbounded extremal solutions is not resolved in the available survey literature.
